transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... hi. I guess I'm just... really exhausted. 

It's been a long year. I've been... well, I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing my dad's lab results. Or holding parts of them back. And... I don't know, no matter how many doctors or people in my family tell me the numbers are fine, they aren't. I know the chart doesn't match what I actually saw. 

Trying to get anyone to listen is just... it's wearing me down.
Aside from your concerns about your dad's lab results, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things, or sensing presences that others don't seem to notice?
No. Um... I don't hear voices or see things. Nothing like that.
How long have you been feeling convinced that your dad's lab results are being changed or withheld—weeks, months, longer?
About a year. Um... basically since his medical problems started. He had to start going to a lot of appointments, getting labs done all the time... so, yeah. A year.
Aside from this situation with your dad's labs, do you generally find yourself distrustful or suspicious of other people's motives in your everyday life, even before this past year?
No. Not really. I mean... I trust people fine. It's just this one thing with the clinic. Before this, everything was normal.
Over this past year, have you also been feeling persistently sad, low, or down, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
No, not really. I mean... I still do my normal stuff. I'm just focused on getting the truth about his labs.
Aside from this issue with your dad's labs, has your ability to work, maintain relationships, or take care of daily responsibilities been affected this past year?
No. Everything else is fine. I mean... I still go to my phlebotomy shifts. I pay my bills, take care of myself... do what I need to do. It's just the clinic that's the problem.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a single, fixed, non-bizarre delusion (belief that clinic staff are falsifying/withholding her father's lab results) persisting for about one year. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech/behavior, no negative symptoms, and mood symptoms are absent (ruling out mood disorder with psychotic features or schizophrenia, which requires broader psychotic symptomatology or functional decline). Functioning is preserved outside the delusional theme (continues work, self-care, relationships), and the delusion is plausible in content (though excessive/incorrigible), consistent with Delusional Disorder, persecutory/somatic-adjacent type.
